title: Demurrage and Detention Free Time: how the final invoice of a container record is computed
content:
## Scope

This policy of the AHL Demurrage and Detention Free Time category sets the general basis on which the final demurrage and detention invoice of a per-container record is computed: chargeable days, the split between demurrage and detention days, charge slabs, the dangerous-goods uplift, the invoice lines written and the minimum invoice.

## Clauses in force

1. The final invoice of a record is computed once its last clock has stopped.
2. The chargeable days of a clock are its days used beyond its free days; a clock that has not used more than its free days has no chargeable day.
3. **Separate clock model.** The chargeable days of the demurrage clock are billed at demurrage rates and those of the detention clock at detention rates, and the slabs restart on each clock.
4. **Combined clock model.** The chargeable days follow the end of the merged free time, and each chargeable day is billed at demurrage rates while the container is inside the terminal and at detention rates while it is outside:
   - on import, days up to and including the full gate-out date are demurrage days and later days are detention days;
   - on export, days up to and including the full gate-in date are detention days and later days are demurrage days.
5. The n-th chargeable day falls in slab 1 while n is at most the slab 1 length, in slab 2 while n is at most the slab 1 length plus the slab 2 length, in slab 3 while n is at most the total of the three slab lengths, and in slab 4 afterwards.
6. When the booking's cargo type is dangerous goods, demurrage days only are increased by the product's dangerous-goods uplift percentage.
7. One demurrage line and one detention line are written, each with its chargeable days, the first and last billed day and the total of its day rates rounded to the cent. A line with no chargeable day is not written.
8. When the two lines together are below the product's minimum invoice, nothing is invoiced and the record is settled.

## Clauses no longer in force

- "Each day is billed at the rate of its clock type, slab and the rate class of the container given by the equipment class map." This clause is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current rate-class basis for the final demurrage and detention lines.
- On a combined clock, "the slab position of a day is counted across the whole sequence of chargeable days." This clause is **no longer in force**; it has been superseded by the current slab-count basis for the final demurrage and detention lines.

The remaining clauses above, including the dangerous-goods increase of demurrage days in clause 6, stay in force.

## Chargeable days and slab days in words

- Chargeable days of a clock: the days used less the free days, and never fewer than none.
- Days in slab 1: the chargeable days, but no more than the slab 1 length.
- Days in slab 2: the chargeable days beyond the slab 1 length, but no more than the slab 2 length.
- Days in slab 3: the chargeable days beyond the first two slab lengths, but no more than the slab 3 length.
- Days in slab 4: every chargeable day beyond the three slab lengths together.

## Worked example (hypothetical slab lengths of 4, 4 and 8 days, used only to show the split)

| Chargeable days on the clock | Slab 1 | Slab 2 | Slab 3 | Slab 4 |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 12 | 4 | 4 | 4 | 0 |
| 25 | 4 | 4 | 8 | 9 |

Under the separate clock model the slabs restart on each clock: an import record with 3 chargeable demurrage days and 7 chargeable detention days counts its demurrage days as slab positions 1 to 3 and its detention days, separately, as positions 1 to 7.

## Points of judgement

**Q: The demurrage clock stayed within free time but the detention clock ran over. How many lines are written?**
A: Only the detention line; a line with no chargeable day is not written.

**Q: Both lines together come to less than the product's minimum invoice. What happens?**
A: Nothing is invoiced and the record is settled.
